text:
sarah_customer: hey team — hitting a weird issue with streaming from our Dedicated instance (private deployment in us-west-2). Started ~yesterday evening after a router firmware update in our corporate network. Symptoms: SSE stream yields a few partial JSON chunks, then connection drops. Client reconnects and sometimes gets duplicated partial outputs. Logs show intermittent 499 / ECONNRESET on the server side. request id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e

maria_support: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the exact error lines from the server? also which customer plan (dedicated/private) and whether ingress is on-prem?

sarah_customer: dedicated (reserved pool), private control plane, ingress is an on-prem nginx reverse proxy maintained by our infra team. repro is basically:

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.private.example.com/v1/stream?model=rw-1-big"
```

server log snippet around the failure: 

```
[2026-03-12T22:14:07Z] INFO stream start req=rq_0a1b2c3d4e client=10.0.5.12
[2026-03-12T22:14:09Z] WARN sse: wrote 128 bytes, ack pending
[2026-03-12T22:14:09Z] ERROR sse: write failed req=rq_0a1b2c3d4e err=write tcp 10.0.5.23:443->10.0.5.12:52344: write: broken pipe
[2026-03-12T22:14:09Z] INFO connection closed req=rq_0a1b2c3d4e code=499
```

jun_infra: can you capture a tcpdump from the ingress side and the server side? Also what's your MTU on the VPC/subnet and on the on-prem appliance? corp proxies often clamp MSS and fragment chunks.

sarah_customer: mtus: VPC 9001 (jumbo), on-prem firewall reports MTU 1500, internal nginx box shows 1460. We suspect the corp proxy (they use a packet-inspection appliance) in front of nginx. tcpdump attached in ticket (I uploaded to ticket 5872). Pattern I saw: event frames get split mid-json, like `{"text":"Hel` then next chunk `lo\n","idx":...}`; some clients treat that as malformed and close.

alex_eng: this reads like middlebox-induced chunk fragmentation. SSE expects the server to send complete text/event-stream frames, but HTTP chunking can still split physically. Most browsers/clients handle chunks reassembling, but some corporate proxies do weird buffering or close idle connections if they see no EOL sequences for a while. Two quick asks: 1) can you turn off `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_http_version 1.1` on nginx (and `chunked_transfer_encoding on`) to preserve streaming? 2) can you try lowering the server's write buffer to emit smaller-but-frequent writes so the proxy doesn't hold data until a threshold?

maria_support: for support escalation we also need to know if this is causing billing spikes (reconnect loops). sarah — do you see repeated connect attempts from the same client leading to token usage inflation?

sarah_customer: yes, we saw ~3x token usage for that endpoint during spikes. Our app retries quickly, so loops happened. Also one customer complained about duplicated partial outputs. Please advise credits.

ingress-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-20260312-5872. Pager duty: oncall_eng alerted.

jun_infra: quick repro from our side with a simulated proxy that clamps MSS to 1200 produced identical mid-chunk splits. Reproducer steps:

1) run a TCP proxy that sets `--mss 1200` and forwards to the private ingress
2) curl -N the SSE endpoint
3) observe `Content-Type: text/event-stream` frames split inside a JSON payload

We dumped bytes with `tcpdump -s0 -w sse.pcap` and saw segments cutting across JSON.

alex_eng: probable root cause summary: your corporate middlebox/MSS clamping + nginx buffering semantics cause fragmented TCP segments that some client stacks treat as separate SSE events or closing frames. Some mitigations:
- On nginx ingress: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection "";`
- Ensure the on-prem appliance doesn't alter `Transfer-Encoding` or add content-length/sniffing.
- Server-side: send heartbeat comments `: keepalive\n\n` every 10s to keep middleboxes happy and force flushes.
- Client-side: make the client robust to partial frames (reassemble stream) and dedupe by event id.

maria_support: sarah — our ops team can ship a small patch you can apply to nginx. We can also provide a short-lived config change to the dedicated ingress to emit smaller writes (rate-limited flush). Would you like us to try the nginx change first or do you want us to coordinate with your on-prem infra to change firewall MSS?

sarah_customer: let's try nginx change first since our infra can restart nginx quickly. Also please apply a one-time credit to offset the spike — we consumed credits due to rapid reconnects.

maria_support: acknowledged. I'll open a billing credit request and assign ops to produce an nginx config diff.

alex_eng: nginx diff we tested:

```nginx
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_pass https://backend;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
}
# also enable tcp_nopush off at OS level if you see coalescing issues
```

jun_infra: added: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` as an optional mitigation for PMTU blackholes. If the corp appliance is actively clamping MSS, you might still need them to change it.

sarah_customer: applied nginx diff, restarted. Immediate improvement: clients now get full JSON events and disconnects dropped to near-zero. We'll keep this for 48h and monitor. Thanks. :raised_hands:

maria_support: billing ticket created (BILL-9013) to credit the spike; ops change rolled into a canary on your ingress. I'll follow up in 24h with final credit.

alex_eng: follow-ups for product: consider adding a streaming compatibility doc for private deployments (best nginx settings, recommended keepalive comments, and guidance on MSS/clamping). Also add a diagnostic script that customers can run to detect mid-chunk fragmentation.

sarah_customer: will report back after 48h. appreciate the quick help!

ingress-bot: INC-20260312-5872 status -> resolved (mitigated by nginx config); assigned to follow-up: alex_eng for docs and jun_infra for diagnostic script.

maria_support: closing the escalation in support tracker but leaving billing & docs follow-ups open. :white_check_mark:
